source.stem: Decide whether the following statements are correct. Mark “√” for correct answers and “×” for wrong answers. (1) Objects that can move must be living things.

hinge.title: Explain why a purely lunar calendar does not keep the same months aligned with the same seasons year after year.

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: lunar calendar is the same as its neighbouring term in this chapter, so the decision does not change.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: The decision still holds even if we ignore this condition: A lunar calendar uses the day as the basic unit and lunar months based on Moon phases.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: the lunar year ends earlier than the seasonal cycle -> the same lunar months no  happens first, and that produces 12 Moon phase cycles total fewer days than the seasonal year.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: This rule applies even when A lunar calendar uses the day as the basic unit and lunar months based on Moon phases is not true.

intelligence.enrichment: Twelve lunar months make a lunar year of 354 days, while the seasons repeat in about 365 days, so lunar months shift relative to the seasons in successive years. 12 Moon phase cycles total fewer days than the seasonal year -> the lunar year ends earlier than the seasonal cycle -> the same lunar months no longer match the same seasons. The learner correctly applies this rule: Twelve lunar months make a lunar year of 354 days, while the seasons repeat in about 365 days, so lunar months shift relative to the seasons in successive years. Twelve months always make one year that matches the seasons, no matter how the months are defined.
